scope: Five new exact production Core migration/archive recovery regressions plus retained first failing archive regression; not a whole-suite/native/release qualification
priorSuccessfulTests: Prior 47 Core tests retained separately. These five new exact scopes do not resolve the remaining G3/G4/G5 coverage gaps.

firstArchiveFailure.name: core::tests::v1_migration_verified_file_keeps_physical_id_and_cursor_when_archived
firstArchiveFailure.assertion: migration must adopt a verified same-file physical key before archive; key before move was ""
firstArchiveFailure.retention: Original tool-session failure is retained, not relabeled passed. Current receipt separately records the later success.

fixture.committedCursor: EOF with exact last_start, nonempty line hash and old JSON context lacking live_cursor
fixture.storedFacts: Stable native identity/digest/serialized facts, original physical record offsets/hashes, source identity and explicit preferences asserted before/after migration and restart
fixture.replay: A real copied JSONL is read by Core.scan; copied physical records must be observed, so unchanged old totals alone cannot satisfy the assertion
fixture.privacy: Self-created content-free temporary fixture; no model call, account bridge or real Codex source mutation

ddlFailure.injection: Only the self-created v1 fixture has a preexisting source_capabilities(fixture_marker) table, causing real migration 002 CREATE failure after six ALTERs and collection_channels CREATE
ddlFailure.productionEntry: Core::open returns the actual SQLite already-exists error
rollbackAssertions: source_files has no partially added source/channel/OS key columns
collection_channels CREATE before the error is rolled back
original and VACUUM INTO backup pass integrity_check
ddlFailure.recovery: Copy the readable backup into a separate private data directory, explicitly remove only the test-injected obstruction in that copy, then production Core::open/scan/restart preserves 1700 tokens and two responses; failed original remains untouched

productionFix.location: same-path physical-file identity validation in the existing per-source transaction
productionFix.verifiedLegacyIdentity: Only an empty OS key with nonzero committed offset within current length, valid start, nonempty hash and successful committed anchor check may adopt the current file handle identity
productionFix.unknownContinuity: Empty/invalid anchor, truncation or replacement without proven continuity retires the old path while retaining old facts/cursor; current physical file receives a new observed row and follows its own later archive move
productionFix.nonemptyIdentity: Existing nonempty OS key is never overwritten; mismatched physical file uses the existing replacement path

limitations: The failure is a real DDL error in a private fixture, not an OS process-kill or installed upgrade interruption.
The fixture covers supported v1 physical storage and verified native metering, not every historical JSON payload or source format.

The two first G2 tests passed before the narrow reader key-adoption fix; the failing archive regression and both new safety guards passed after it. This is scoped composite evidence, not a rerun of all 52 Core tests.
No migration schema, metering identity, Core settings authority, query, dist or main release EXE was modified for these tests/fix.
Only reader.rs and core/tests.rs were changed by this work; concurrent capability-report and desktop-worker changes have separate owners/evidence.
G3/G4/G5 broader notification/result, time/filter boundary, retention/export/native gaps remain separately tracked; no whole M4 claim.
